## Overview

Cloudflare introduced Search for Agents on November 25, 2026, a feature that lets site operators turn on AI-powered search for their domain with a single dashboard toggle, according to a [Cloudflare blog post](https://blog.cloudflare.com/search-for-agents/) by Celso Martinho and Gabriel Massadas. The post describes the feature as putting the setup of an AI Search instance "behind a toggle in your Cloudflare dashboard," so that turning it on for a zone makes Cloudflare "create your A...

recommendations: Merge the PR; publish a corrections record for the dropped co-author in the Overview byline.
developers.cloudflare.com added to config/source_allowlist.txt in this commit.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean News-category writeup (680 words, within the 400-1200 range) with a clear Overview/What changed/Discovery/Availability/What we don't know structure. The writer flagged a possible discrepancy between the two Cloudflare sources on 'beta' language and asked for it to be checked carefully; on verification the discrepancy is real and the article already handles it correctly (see factual_accuracy below), so no change was needed there.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and snapshot sha256 hashes verified by rehashing the decompressed files on disk: source-0.html.gz (blog.cloudflare.com) = aff42e3018054bdcfc835bac514a689b9cbc70eb37d9ba0772200e52fda82f9d, matches manifest. source-1.html.gz (developers.cloudflare.com) = d6145f6234da7c773a5d34ecc7e5cb73c01d0fc4ec790a6e427be8aa51d5817e, matches manifest. developers.cloudflare.com was not on config/source_allowlist.txt; confirmed it is Cloudflare's own official developer-documentation subdomain (branded 'Cloudflare Docs', same organization as the already-allowlisted blog.cloudflare.com, structured data in the page identifies the publisher as Cloudflare) and added it to the allowlist in this review's commit with a justification comment, per the 'Source allowlist and unreachable sources' procedure. Anthropic disclosure: not required - Anthropic/Claude is not the subject, headline, summary, lead, or credited anywhere in this article; contributor_model is recorded only in provenance metadata.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Systematically checked every specific claim against the raw decompressed HTML text of both snapshots (not a summary): (1) Nov 25, 2026 launch date and feature description - confirmed via blogDate metadata '2026-11-25T14:00:00.000Z' and body text ('puts that setup behind a toggle in your Cloudflare dashboard... create your AI Search instance, start indexing your content'). (2) Pre-existing AI Search / manual setup friction quotes - confirmed verbatim. (3) Instance naming pattern 'search-for-agents-<ZONE_ID>', crawl page limit 100,000 pages, crawl depth five link hops, 24-hour sync interval - all confirmed verbatim in the dev-docs settings table (source-1). (4) /.well-known/search endpoint, <meta name="agent:endpoint"> tag, and the YAML front-matter example for Markdown for Agents-enabled zones - confirmed verbatim in source-0. (5) The 'follows naturally from Markdown for Agents' quote, the HTTP QUERY / RFC 10008 / James Snell / June 2026 claims, and the idempotency language - confirmed verbatim in source-0 ('IETF Proposed Standard, incidentally coauthored by our own James Snell, published in June 2026 as RFC 10008'). (6) curl and undici cited as adopting/discussing QUERY - confirmed verbatim. (7) 'Results come back as retrieved Markdown content... not an AI-generated answer' and the 'agent already has an AI model and a conversation' quote - confirmed verbatim in source-0. (8) Bot management/AI Crawl Control/WAF settings gating access - confirmed verbatim in source-0 ('subject to your domain settings (e.g. your bot management settings, AI Crawl Control and web application firewall (WAF) configurations)'). THE FLAGGED DISCREPANCY: Verified directly in raw text, not just the manifest excerpt. Blog post (source-0) body prose uses 'available to all customers, including Free (with limits)' and 'Starting today, Search for Agents is available to all customers' - neither sentence contains the word 'beta'; the only 'beta' hit on the page is an alphabetical sitewide tag-cloud entry ('Best Practices...Beta...Better Internet') unrelated to this post (the post's own blogTags metadata is 'Agents,AI,AI Search' - no Beta tag). Developer docs (source-1) body prose states 'Search for Agents is available in beta on all plans' verbatim, and the page's own left-nav sidebar shows a 'Beta' badge next to the current page's own entry (aria-current="page"). This is a genuine, verifiable disagreement between Cloudflare's two official pages about the same feature's rollout status, not a writer misreading. The article's dedicated 'Availability' section reports both positions with direct quotes and correct attribution to each source, states plainly that 'the two pages do not reconcile this difference,' and does not resolve the conflict by fabricating an explanation - this is the correct handling per the claim-accuracy policy on source disagreements. No correction needed on this point. ONE ISSUE FOUND: the Overview's opening sentence attributes the Cloudflare blog post to 'Celso Martinho and Gabriel Massadas' only. The raw snapshot's byline (rendered HTML, not just metadata) lists three co-authors with linked author pages: 'Celso Martinho, Gabriel Massadas, and Nelson Duarte' (page metadata independently confirms blogAuthorCount:3). The article drops the third credited co-author. This is an incomplete attribution in the lead paragraph, but it is a subordinate detail (who wrote the Cloudflare post) rather than the article's core claim (what Cloudflare launched and how it works), so it does not gut the lead. Filing a corrections record rather than rejecting.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive throughout; every characterization is hedged with 'the company says' / 'the post says' / 'according to.' No sensationalism, no unsourced editorializing, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-11/ for prior Cloudflare coverage. Two unrelated Cloudflare articles exist this month (post-quantum GeoKey Manager closed beta on 11-06, and the Vite ecosystem fund on 11-12) - neither overlaps with Search for Agents. This is a genuinely new topic with no duplicate coverage.
concerns: Lead paragraph (Overview) credits only two of the Cloudflare blog post's three co-authors, omitting Nelson Duarte, who is listed in the rendered byline and in the page's blogAuthorCount:3 metadata.
recommendations: Writers should check the full rendered byline (and blogAuthorCount metadata where present) rather than reading only the first names visible in a quoted excerpt, to avoid dropping co-authors on multi-author posts.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Overturning the automated REJECT: the single error-severity finding was a false-positive prompt-injection match on a routine documentation sidebar nav link ('Reranking... System prompt... Filtering' - a list of Cloudflare's own AI Search configuration page titles, not an instruction directed at an AI agent), and the allowlist warning has been resolved by adding developers.cloudflare.com (Cloudflare's own docs domain) to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment in this review's commit. Substantively, this is a strong, thoroughly-sourced News piece: every specific and quote was independently verified against the raw snapshot text, and the writer's flagged beta/no-beta discrepancy between Cloudflare's blog and developer docs is a genuine disagreement between the two sources (confirmed directly in raw text) that the article already reports correctly with attribution to both, rather than a misreading - no correction needed on that point. The one real issue is a dropped co-author (Nelson Duarte) in the Overview's byline attribution, a subordinate detail that does not affect the article's core claims; recoverable with a single corrections note. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, well-verified vendor feature launch of interest to a defined developer/AI-agent-tooling audience, but a single-vendor product announcement without independent coverage, not a broad-audience or industry-shifting story.
